DESTRUCTOR ORDER IS THE REPRODUCIBLE ONE: the cartridge puts D1 at 0x0210788c BELOW D0 at 0x02107920 and carries no D2. mwccarm 2004/b56 emits D1-then-D0 for an inline in-class destructor, so the pair stays inside the licensed run and this TU promotes whole at 40/40 -- there is no held-out subset. include/dScMgRoulette_c.h's destructor was moved inline for exactly this reason; declared out of line it emits D2/D0/D1 plus a D2 the ROM lacks.

PRAGMA BLOCKER RETIRED BY MEASUREMENT -- AND THE MEASUREMENT CORRECTS MY OWN FIRST READING OF IT. notes/data/tu-promotion-queue.tsv lists this class with pragma:1, and tubuild create's emitted note says optimize_for_size and opt_propagation are FILE-GLOBAL last-wins and refuses to carry them. Four controls, each a full tubuild verify: (a) both shard pragmas bracketed around their own members -> 40/40 MATCH; (b) both pragmas DELETED outright -> 40/40 MATCH; (c) `#pragma optimize_for_size on` at file scope with no closing `off` -> 23/40, 17 DIFF; (d) `#pragma optimize_for_size on`/`off` bracketed around func_ov006_02108d28, one of the 17 members control (c) proved to be size-sensitive -> 40/40 MATCH. (c) proves the compile is live and that this pragma really does move bytes; (d) then proves the bracket did NOT bind -- had it bound, 02108d28 would have gone DIFF. The trailing `off` restored the default for the entire file. So mwccarm 2004/b56 IS file-global last-wins for optimize_for_size, notes/agents/roles/writer.md is right, and control (a) proved nothing about positionality: it passed only because control (b) shows both members match at the plain -O4,p defaults anyway. The pragma:1 blocker is therefore a phantom for this class -- the shards' pragmas were belt-and-braces -- and the promoted TU carries no pragma at all. This is a partial retraction of the claim an earlier draft of this manifest made (that brackets bind positionally); the retraction is the measurement, not an opinion.

DEFER_CODEGEN: MEASURED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT USED. Repeating control (d) above with `#pragma defer_codegen off` as the first line of the TU flips the verdict: 39/40 with the DIFF being EXACTLY the bracketed func_ov006_02108d28 and nothing else. So defer_codegen off does make a positional optimize_for_size bracket bind, which extends the dScMgMemory2_c writer's finding (measured there on opt_propagation and opt_loop_invariants) to a third pragma. It is not used here for two reasons. First, this TU needs no pragma at all -- see control (b). Second, the same run flips emission order: with deferral ON mwcc emits .text in reverse source order, which is why this file is written in DESCENDING ROM order and why `tubuild verify` reports ROM-ascending emission; with `defer_codegen off` the same file reported '38 ordinal pair(s) NOT in ROM order' and linkcheck [4b/8] would refuse it. The two are coupled: adopting defer_codegen off means rewriting the TU in ASCENDING ROM order. Either layout is admissible, but they cannot be mixed.
